title: Turn your kid's favorite books into phonics readers
summary: A parent built a free phonics reading app for his six-year-old; connected agents like Claude or ChatGPT can type in owned books or write stories using only sounds she knows.
agent_role: The agent reads a book PDF or photos, types the story into the app or writes a new one, checks each word against the child's known sounds, adds pictures and shows the parent the result.
outcome: The author says the app is free, open source, and his 12-year-old son wrote the first story.
what_they_did: A father built a reading app for his daughter after she finished a phonics game. She taps any word to hear its sounds. Parents set which sounds the child knows. They can connect their own AI agent, hand it a PDF or phone photos of a book they own, and have it import the book or write new stories.
how_it_went: The author reports the agent checks its own words, adds pictures and shows the parent the result, kept private to their account. Included stories are free to reuse.
worth_knowing: The built-in checker rejects any word the child can't sound out yet; the author's advice is to rewrite the story rather than loosen the sounds.
prompt: Using the Yara Reads connection, import the book in [PDF or photos of a book I own] for my child. My child knows these sounds: [list of sounds] and these tricky words: [list]. Check every word against what they know. Where a word uses a sound they haven't learned, suggest a simpler rewrite and list the changes for me. Add simple pictures for each page. Show me the finished draft and wait for my approval before saving it to my account.

curation.rationale: A parent built a phonics reader whose agent connection lets Claude or ChatGPT import owned books or write stories limited to the sounds a child knows, then check every word; a novel education workflow, though the agent outcome is lightly evidenced.
